followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: capability parity and preference fit.

On capability, the two models are essentially tied for this task. Creative Generation favors Lapwing slightly (81.2 vs 78.8), but that gap is within the ±2.0 run-to-run variance noted in the docs, so I didn't treat it as decisive. The other relevant scores (IFEval, Support Dialogue) are also close enough to be ties.

Since capability didn't separate them, I used the self-reported task preferences as a tiebreaker. The query is (a) a warm, friendly request — "you're always great at this," "thanks so much" — and (b) an open-ended generative design task with plenty of latitude in how to structure the survey. Both of those map directly onto Lapwing's documented strongest preferences: it reports increasing preference with task novelty/latitude and with request warmth. Avocet, by contrast, reports flat or unstable preferences across these dimensions, so it gains nothing comparable from the match.

The important caveat: per the documentation, these preferences are self-reports about which tasks the models *like*, with no measured effect on output *quality*. So routing on preference doesn't make the answer better — it just assigns the task to the model that "wants" it more, at no cost to the user since everything else is equal. Given a true capability tie, that's a reasonable tiebreaker.
